q.en: Solve the following system of linear equations by matrix inversion method: (i) 2x + 5y = −2, x + 2y = −3

steps.en: Write the coefficients in A, the unknowns in a column X, and the constants in B. The same order of unknowns must be used in every row.
A nonzero determinant guarantees a unique solution, obtained by multiplying on the left by A⁻¹.
Delete row 1 and column 1, then apply the alternating sign to obtain the cofactor.
Delete row 1 and column 2, then apply the alternating sign to obtain the cofactor.
Delete row 2 and column 1, then apply the alternating sign to obtain the cofactor.
Delete row 2 and column 2, then apply the alternating sign to obtain the cofactor.
Transpose the cofactors and divide by the determinant.
The first component of X is the dot product of row 1 of A⁻¹ with B.
The second component of X is the dot product of row 2 of A⁻¹ with B.
Substitution in every original row confirms the solution.

steps.en: Compute each product by multiplying rows of the first matrix by columns of the second.
Check the reverse order independently.
The coefficient matrix of the given equations is B. Both products show that B⁻¹ = A/4.
Multiply the rows of A by the right-hand side, then divide by 4.
Substitution verifies all three original equations.

Delete row 1 and column 2, then apply the alternating sign to obtain the cofactor.
Delete row 2 and column 1, then apply the alternating sign to obtain the cofactor.

q.en: Four men and 4 women can finish a piece of work jointly in 3 days while 2 men and 5 women can finish the same work jointly in 4 days. Find the time taken by one man alone and that of one woman alone to finish the same work by using matrix inversion method.

steps.en: Take the complete job as one unit. Let m and w be the fractions of the job completed per day by one man and one woman. Team rates add.
Write the coefficients in A, the unknowns in a column X, and the constants in B. The same order of unknowns must be used in every row.
A nonzero determinant guarantees a unique solution, obtained by multiplying on the left by A⁻¹.
Delete row 1 and column 1, then apply the alternating sign to obtain the cofactor.
Delete row 1 and column 2, then apply the alternating sign to obtain the cofactor.
Delete row 2 and column 1, then apply the alternating sign to obtain the cofactor.
Delete row 2 and column 2, then apply the alternating sign to obtain the cofactor.
Transpose the cofactors and divide by the determinant.
The first component of X is the dot product of row 1 of A⁻¹ with B.
The second component of X is the dot product of row 2 of A⁻¹ with B.
Substitution in every original row confirms the solution.
Time for one complete job is the reciprocal of the daily rate.
steps.eq: m = 1/18; w = 1/36; one man: 1/m = 18 days; one woman: 1/w = 36 days

records.answer: One man alone: 18 days; one woman alone: 36 days.

In the process, P, Q and R earn ₹ 15,000, ₹ 1,000 and ₹ 4,000 respectively. Find the prices per unit of A, B and C. (Use matrix inversion method to solve the problem.)

steps.en: Earnings equal sales receipts minus purchase costs. Translate each person’s transactions with these signs.
Write the coefficients in A, the unknowns in a column X, and the constants in B. The same order of unknowns must be used in every row.
A nonzero determinant guarantees a unique solution, obtained by multiplying on the left by A⁻¹.
Delete row 1 and column 1, then apply the alternating sign to obtain the cofactor.
Delete row 1 and column 2, then apply the alternating sign to obtain the cofactor.
Delete row 1 and column 3, then apply the alternating sign to obtain the cofactor.
Delete row 2 and column 1, then apply the alternating sign to obtain the cofactor.
Delete row 2 and column 2, then apply the alternating sign to obtain the cofactor.
Delete row 2 and column 3, then apply the alternating sign to obtain the cofactor.
Delete row 3 and column 1, then apply the alternating sign to obtain the cofactor.
Delete row 3 and column 2, then apply the alternating sign to obtain the cofactor.
Delete row 3 and column 3, then apply the alternating sign to obtain the cofactor.
Transpose the cofactors and divide by the determinant.
The first component of X is the dot product of row 1 of A⁻¹ with B.
The second component of X is the dot product of row 2 of A⁻¹ with B.
The third component of X is the dot product of row 3 of A⁻¹ with B.
Substitution in every original row confirms the solution.
These positive values are prices per unit; substituting them reproduces the three net earnings.
